risks.quote: GenAI has a large carbon footprint and consumes large amounts of energy and water, which have consequences for our environment.
An over-reliance on GenAI may hinder your own critical skills development.
GenAI tools are known to produce false, inaccurate, or misleading information, called ‘hallucinations’.
Where these data lakes contain biases or misinformation, the output of these platforms may perpetuate these.
when using GenAI without proper accreditation, you could inadvertently plagiarise or breach the copyright of someone’s work.

Do not enter personally identifiable or sensitive information into GenAI platforms. Some platforms store the interactions, which may constitute a data breach under the Data Protection Act and UK GDPR 2018.
GenAI tools are being used to produce deepfakes. These are text, images, or videos which have been digitally altered to deliberately mislead or spread false and defamatory information.
The use of workers in poorer economies for data-labelling tasks.

The inequitable access to GenAI platforms within our University community, broadly and globally, creating a further divide between those who can afford to pay for the latest GenAI models and those who cannot.
As we integrate GenAI into our daily lives, it is essential to consider its potential impact on our mental and emotional wellbeing.

responsibilities.quote: Always verify GenAI outputs' truthfulness and accuracy.

GenAI platforms don't take responsibility for the output they produce; you can read the terms and conditions of a platform to verify this. Any output generated should be cross-referenced for accuracy, using authoritative sources, by you as the author of your work.
GenAI tools pose ethical issues that you should consider when using them for work, research, and leisure.
GenAI should be used in accordance with the guidance given here.
Ensure you are familiar with CCCU’s Academic Integrity Policy.
If you need to report a data breach to our Information Governance team, use the data breach report form.
